Alexander Clavel.fact: Alexander Clavel (17 December 1805 – 22 February 1873), also recorded as Alexander Clavel-Oswald and Alexander Clavel-Linder in 19th-century Basel sources, was a French-born Swiss textile industrialist and silk dyer who, in 1859, began producing the synthetic dye fuchsine in Basel. Alexander Clavel.question: The move marked a shift of colour chemistry to _____'s outskirts and foreshadowed the city's industrial expansion
Alexander Clavel.fact: Complaints about fumes from arsenic-based processes led Basel authorities to restrict aniline-red production; in 1864 Clavel moved the works to the Klybeckstrasse on the Rhine, creating a "Laboratorium für Fabrikation von Anilin- und anderen Farben" [Laboratory for the production of aniline and other dyes].
